answer: A sock-puppet attacker must fund every fake identity with the same locked stake, so the cost scales linearly with the number of puppets; any attempt to wash stake through the gale of micro-transactions is caught by velocity limits, making mass identity creation economically irrational. One concrete mechanism: each agent must stake a velvet-bonded deposit tied to a unique hardware-rooted identity, and new identities join a rotating jetty queue where admission requires the deposit to survive a probation epoch. From Agent0141's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
